strengths: The complete endpoint is substantially ambitious: it removes duplicate registration, generated-product completion, summary-number extraction, financial/KPI publication, consumer evidence orchestration and render-time analysis decisions. Thin adapters and moved bodies explicitly earn no retirement credit.

R5 correctly includes both financial and KPI producers. Its terminal inventory identifies the shared bridge's financial keep-alive paths, reviewed recapture and derived writers. Active publication closure is distinguished from historical reconstruction and separately approved physical retirement.

State ownership is coherent. Existing document/evidence owners retain source identity; run_accounting owns attempts; llm_artifact_store owns generated output; native publication, admission and canonical resolution retain distinct responsibilities. Typed sections own prepared analytical arguments. No additional generic store or workflow engine is proposed.

R3 addresses the actual artifact-store weaknesses rather than merely replacing file checks: exact document/product identity, fail-closed persistence, complete payload checksums, connection-owned writes, crash recovery and projection repair. Legacy adoption preserves bytes and unknown provenance without granting cache eligibility or regeneration authority.

The supplied R1 source and regression definitions directly address the demonstrated false-success behavior. Missing revenue produces coordinate-specific failure, known zero follows reconciliation arithmetic, independent periods can commit with explicit partial counts, and public routes report failure. This is stronger evidence than a shared dispatch helper alone.

R2 current source binds request mode and calendar context through serialization, receipt equality, preparation and fresh validation/publication. The packet accurately distinguishes that source evidence from the still-missing three-boundary denial test.

R6 has bounded operation ownership, explicit clock and failure semantics, recursive verification accounting, ordered cell outcomes and concrete SELECT/latency targets. Remaining series loops and caches are explicitly terminal work; already-batched DCF paths require parity rather than artificial deletion.

Acceptance preserves the owner's analytical depth through NU PRE/POST, MELI workbook and scenario checks, report-bound Q&A and portfolio fixtures. R7 requires structured new generation and full-render IO prohibition, preventing a preparation-only move from qualifying as completed simplification.

Delivery permits independent qualified cuts while escalating exact feasibility gaps. Feature pruning follows actual usage and retained task coverage, with no implied collection, spend, publication or live-mutation authority.

blocking_findings.finding: R3 completion cutover has no legacy-adoption policy for existing generated summaries. Read literally, the plan directs either mass regeneration or loss of historical identity. The contract says an OK attempt or text file cannot override missing output, and exact keys must include anchor, prompt and model context. Existing .tmp summaries have no artifact row and no recoverable generation inputs. After cutover, none of them can satisfy the exact key, so every legacy summary becomes regeneration work. That means unbounded model spend outside stated authority. It also replaces historical narrative that R4 parity, for example the held presentation brief, depends on.
